title: Shell script
description: Convert with Bash, curl, and jq.

sections.title: Save as convert.sh
paragraphs: Requires curl with --fail-with-body support and jq. Use an HTTPS base URL outside loopback. The script checks for existing output before starting; use a dedicated output directory to avoid concurrent writers.
sections.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${CONVRT_API_URL:?Set API URL}"
: "${CONVRT_API_KEY:?Set API key}"
input=${1:?Input file}
target=${2:?Target format}
output=${3:?Output file}
[[ ! -e "$output" ]] || { echo "Output exists" >&2; exit 1; }
job_id=''
cleanup() {
  if [[ -n "$job_id" ]]; then
    curl --silent --show-error --fail --max-time 10 -X DELETE \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVRT_API_KEY" \
      "$CONVRT_API_URL/v1/jobs/$job_id" >/dev/null ||
      echo "Cleanup deferred; retention still applies" >&2
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
job=$(curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body --max-time 60 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVRT_API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@$input" -F "to=$target" "$CONVRT_API_URL/v1/jobs")
job_id=$(jq -er '.id' <<<"$job")
for ((attempt=0; attempt<180; attempt++)); do
  job=$(curl --silent --show-error --fail-with-body --max-time 10 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVRT_API_KEY" "$CONVRT_API_URL/v1/jobs/$job_id")
  status=$(jq -er '.status' <<<"$job")
  if [[ "$status" == succeeded ]]; then
    curl --silent --show-error --fail --max-time 60 \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONVRT_API_KEY" \
      "$CONVRT_API_URL/v1/jobs/$job_id/download" --output "$output"
    exit 0
  fi
  [[ "$status" != failed ]] || { echo "Conversion failed" >&2; exit 1; }
  sleep 1
done
echo "Timed out" >&2
exit 1

sections.title: Before using this in an application
paragraphs: Run the example with a small synthetic input first, using a server whose engines support the chosen route. Set CONVRT_API_URL to your server origin and load CONVRT_API_KEY from the environment. Keep the key out of browser code and committed configuration.
Choose an output directory appropriate for private files. A successful conversion does not imply that the result is safe to publish; your application decides who can access it and when to delete it.
